note.note:
Medical History

- Current health concerns and risk factors:  1 week of sore throat followed by dry cough; exertional shortness of breath starting ~3–4 days ago; mild wheeze; intermittent chest discomfort (present earlier; later clinician phrased as “not chest pain” — conflict noted); initial fever for ~3 days now resolved; intermittent headaches; decreased appetite without weight loss; no hemoptysis; no nasal/sinus congestion; non-smoker; family history of lung cancer (mother); lives in UK (born in US); requested work sick note.
- Relevant family medical history:  Mother with lung cancer. No other conditions reported.
- Medications (including OTC or shared medications):  None reported.
- Immunisation status reviewed:  Not recorded.
- Sexual and reproductive health:  Not recorded.
- Physical activity and nutrition:  Exercises “now and then”; appetite reduced recently; denies weight loss.
- Alcohol, tobacco, and substance use:  Tobacco: non-smoker (rare experimentation); Alcohol: not recorded; Other substances: not recorded; Asbestos exposure: not known.
- Hearing loss or concerns:  Not recorded.
- Mood/mental health (including depression, self-harm risk):  Not recorded.
- Vision problems or recent changes:  Not recorded.
- Family and social relationships, caring responsibilities:  Employed; resides in UK; born in US. Caring responsibilities not recorded.

Examination

- BP, pulse rate and rhythm:  Not recorded.
- Height, weight, BMI, waist circumference (if indicated):  Not recorded.
- Oral exam (including dentition and gums):  Not recorded (video consultation; no throat visualization performed).
- Ear exam (otoscopy, whisper test if needed):  Not recorded.
- Vision/eye exam (basic screen):  Not recorded.
- Urinalysis (dipstick for proteinuria):  Not recorded.

Investigations (as indicated)

- Fasting BGL and lipids (or random BGL if needed):  Not recorded.
- Cervical screening (if eligible and due):  Not recorded.
- STI screen (urine or swab – chlamydia/gonorrhoea if age 15–35):  Not recorded.
- Mammogram (if eligible):  Not recorded.
- Other pathology (e.g., HbA1c, iron studies, Vitamin D):  Not recorded.

Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

- Key findings: Acute onset sore throat progressing to dry cough with initial transient fever; new exertional dyspnea and subjective wheeze; intermittent chest discomfort; non-smoker; mother with lung cancer; appetite reduced without weight loss. No hemoptysis; maintains activity; symptoms variable but non-severe.
- Differential diagnoses (aligned with DDx):
  - Acute viral upper respiratory infection with acute bronchitis (including consideration of COVID-19/influenza) — High likelihood: Symptom progression, initial fever, dry cough, mild wheeze, and improving course without red flags.
  - Post-viral reactive airway disease/new-onset asthma — Moderate likelihood: Dry cough, wheeze, exertional dyspnea following viral illness; atopic background (peanut allergy).
  - Atypical or early community-acquired pneumonia — Low–Moderate likelihood: Initial fever and chest discomfort, but currently afebrile and not systemically unwell; dry cough without sputum.
  - Pulmonary embolism — Low likelihood: Exertional dyspnea and chest discomfort present, but no risk factors; onset with viral symptoms.
- Conflicts noted: Patient initially denied then affirmed shortness of breath; chest pain reported earlier but later phrased by clinician as “you say you don't have any chest pain” — conflicting documentation.
- Working diagnosis: Acute viral URI with acute bronchitis. Monitor for post-viral reactive airway symptoms. Low concern for pneumonia, PE, TB, or lung cancer given current presentation and timeline.

Management Plan

- Advice/treatment provided:
  - Rest, maintain hydration, and use paracetamol (acetaminophen) for symptom relief.
  - Sick note provided for additional days off work.
  - Safety-netting: Seek in-person GP evaluation urgently if dyspnea worsens, sudden change in breathlessness, or other concerning symptoms. Reassess if not improving within 4–5 days.
- Follow-up: Contact a medical professional if not improving as expected or if symptoms worsen. No tests ordered during this teleconsultation.

- Allied health referral (EPC – 10 visits):  Not recorded.
- Reproductive or sexual health clinic referral:  Not recorded.
- Mental health support if indicated (e.g., psychologist, AMS support):  Not recorded.
- CTG registration:  Not recorded.
- Preventive health follow-up booked (e.g., flu vaccine, Pap test):  Not recorded.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)

- Acute viral URI with acute bronchitis — High: Typical 1-week course starting with sore throat, progressing to dry cough; initial fever resolved; mild wheeze/exertional dyspnea; no red flags.
- Post-viral reactive airway disease/new-onset asthma — Moderate: Dry cough, wheeze, exertional dyspnea temporally related to viral illness; atopic history (peanut allergy); no prior asthma history.
- Atypical/community-acquired pneumonia — Low–Moderate: Initial fever and chest discomfort, but afebrile now, no sputum, and not systemically unwell.

Quality checks

- Missing expected elements: Vitals (BP, pulse), respiratory rate, oxygen saturation, temperature; physical exam (chest/throat/ears); BMI/anthropometrics; immunization review (including flu/COVID status); alcohol and other substance use history; sexual and reproductive health history; mental health screening; hearing and vision screening; urinalysis; baseline labs (BGL, lipids) as preventive care.
- Internal contradictions: Shortness of breath initially denied then confirmed; chest pain reported earlier vs later phrasing suggesting no chest pain — conflict noted. Recorded DOB (09-May-2016) inconsistent with adult status — conflict noted.
- Transcript quality: Teleconsultation with some interruptions; limited objective data; no physical examination possible.
